text: Which collection would you choose for "is this word in my dictionary?" over a million words, and why?
choices: A sorted `ArrayList` with binary search, since it uses less memory per element.
A `TreeSet`, since the ordering makes lookups logarithmic rather than linear.
A `HashSet`, because membership is the only operation and it is average constant time.
A `LinkedList`, since dictionaries grow and shrink and linked structures resize cheaply.
explanation: Choose by access pattern. Membership by value with no ordering requirement is exactly what a hash set is for, and O(1) beats the sorted list's O(log n) and the tree's O(log n). The sorted-list option is not absurd — it does use less memory and is cache-friendlier — which is why Chapter 32 says the class is one input to the decision and a measurement is another.
